basic_information.official_title: AN ACT EXTENDING THE AVAILABILITY OF THE GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS ACT OF THE BANGSAMORO UNTIL DECEMBER 31, 2022, EXCEPT PERSONNEL SERVICES AND OTHER ITEMS OF THE MOOE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 47 OF THE GENERAL PROVISIONS OF THE GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS ACT OF THE BANGSAMORO FOR YEARS 2020 AND 2021
signed_by: Atty. Ali Pangalian M. Balindong, Speaker
Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: Immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Gives the region until the end of 2022 to spend leftover money from both the 2020 and 2021 budgets — and until mid-2023 to finish paying for infrastructure already started. Salaries are again excluded.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Two budget years of unspent appropriations were due to lapse. Rather than let projects already funded expire, Parliament extended both at once, 8 days before the 2021 deadline.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Appropriations from 2020 and 2021 stayed obligable until 31 December 2022. Infrastructure and capital outlays from both years could be delivered, inspected and paid up to 30 June 2023. Personnel Services from each year still expired on schedule.
who_will_be_affected: Communities with projects funded in 2020 or 2021
Contractors delivering infrastructure under those budgets
Bangsamoro ministries and offices holding unspent funds
Taxpayers, since the money stayed in its original purposes
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: Took effect immediately on publication in early 2022. Its windows have now closed.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: SPENT AND CLOSED. Leftover 2020 and 2021 money stayed usable through 2022, with infrastructure payments allowed until 30 June 2023. Salaries were not extended either year.
in_practice: 2020 appropriations: available for release and disbursement until 31 December 2022
2021 appropriations: available for obligation until 31 December 2022
Infrastructure and capital outlays from both years: obligable to 31 December 2022, with delivery, inspection and payment by 30 June 2023
Continuing MOOE programmes extended to 31 December 2022
Personnel Services: 2020 money expired 31 December 2020; 2021 money expired 31 December 2021

for_specific_groups.Communities awaiting projects: Work funded in 2020 or 2021 did not have to be cancelled and re-appropriated.
for_specific_groups.Contractors: An extra 6 months beyond the obligation deadline to complete delivery, inspection and payment.
for_specific_groups.Government employees: Nothing changed — salary appropriations lapsed on their original dates.

what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: Historic. The last window closed on 30 June 2023.
what_you_can_do: Read this as budget history — it explains why 2020- and 2021-funded projects were still being paid into 2023
watch_out_for: This is the second extension of the 2020 budget: BAA 14 had already pushed it to the end of 2021, and this act pushed it again to the end of 2022.
No new money, and no change of purpose.
Personnel Services excluded in both years, as in every extension act in this series.

key_terms_explained.Obligation: Committing money to a contract or purchase, as distinct from actually paying it out.
key_terms_explained.MOOE: Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses — the running costs of an office.
key_terms_explained.Capital outlay: Money for lasting things: buildings, vehicles, equipment, infrastructure.
key_terms_explained.MFBM: The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management, which issues the implementing guidelines.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Jumada Al-Ula 23, 1443 / 28 December 2021, approved by the Chief Minister on 7 February 2022.

benefits.headline: Two budget years of project money kept alive instead of lapsing.

direct_benefits.benefit: 2020 and 2021 project and operating money remained spendable through 2022
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Communities and agencies with pending funded work
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Automatic — it changed deadlines, not processes

direct_benefits.benefit: An extra window to 30 June 2023 to complete and pay for infrastructure
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Contractors and the communities awaiting the works

indirect_benefits: Avoided mass cancellation and re-appropriation of already-budgeted work

for_citizens: None. The act governs government spending deadlines.

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management (MFBM), authorised to issue the implementing guidelines
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure of its own.

everyday_scenarios: A road funded in the 2021 budget was still under construction at the end of that year. This act let the money stay obligated through 2022 and be paid out up to 30 June 2023.
An agency with unspent 2021 salary money could not carry it forward — Personnel Services expired on 31 December 2021.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Amends Section 47 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 3 (the FY2020 General Appropriations Act). All appropriations are available for release and disbursement for the purpose specified until 31 December 2022. For FY2020, infrastructure and capital outlays are valid for obligation until 31 December 2022, with delivery, inspection and payment no later than 30 June 2023; continuing programmes under MOOE are likewise obligable until 31 December 2022. Personnel Services remain valid for obligation and disbursement only until 31 December 2020. The MFBM is authorised to issue implementing guidelines.

Section 2 — Amends Section 47 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 15 (the FY2021 General Appropriations Act) in parallel terms. All appropriations are obligable until 31 December 2022. FY2021 infrastructure and capital outlays are valid for obligation until 31 December 2022, with delivery, inspection and payment no later than 30 June 2023; MOOE is valid for obligation and disbursement until 31 December 2022. Personnel Services remain valid only until 31 December 2021.
Section 3 — Repeals or modifies inconsistent laws, decrees, executive issuances, rules and regulations.
Section 4 — Takes effect immediately after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

impact.allocated_budget: No new appropriation. It extends the life of money already appropriated by BAA 3 (FY2020) and BAA 15 (FY2021).
impact.figures_note: The act states no amount — it changes deadlines, not sums.

citizen_questions.a: It moved two deadlines. Money appropriated in the 2020 and 2021 Bangsamoro budgets stayed usable until 31 December 2022, and infrastructure funded in either year could be delivered and paid up to 30 June 2023.
No. It extended the availability of appropriations already made.

Every extension act in this series keeps Personnel Services on its original expiry — 2020 money died at the end of 2020, 2021 money at the end of 2021 — so unspent payroll cannot be carried forward and redirected.
No. The last window it opened closed on 30 June 2023.

display_header.what_this_does: Kept 2020 and 2021 budget money spendable through 2022, with infrastructure payable to mid-2023.
display_header.who_it_affects: Agencies with unspent funds · communities awaiting projects · contractors

views.simple: Extended the 2020 and 2021 Bangsamoro budgets to 31 December 2022, with infrastructure delivery and payment allowed until 30 June 2023, while letting salary appropriations expire on their original dates.
